text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Finance ministry offers to help Dutch companies threatened by bankruptcy due to French truckers' strike. (p1)
- Decline in long-term interest rates in the Netherlands accelerates. (p1)
- National resources and demographic institute RPD's report says Schiphol airport could be moved to an island which could be built in the North Sea. (p1)
- Mobile phone company Libertel demands new frequencies from state, although excluded until 2000 by contract. (p1)
- Dispensing chemists' cooperative OPG launches giant claim against government to compensate revenue losses due to pharmaceutical pricing act. (p3)
- Transport group Nedlloyd to change management structure. (p3)
- Bankers Trust, major shareholder in Australia's TNT, accepts Dutch PTT's bid. (p4)
- Brokerage Van der Moolen chairman Hans Kroon sells stake. (p13)
VOLKSKRANT
- Introduction price of sleeping room furniture producer Beter Bed set at Dfl 28. (p2)
- Potato starch concern Avebe takes over starch producer Latenstein Zetmeel of Nijmegen. (p2)
- Friesland Bank intends to stay small, but does not exclude merger with Van Lanschot Bankiers. (p2)
- Dutch truckers stuck in France during strike did not receive enough help from foreign affairs ministry, says traffic association TLN. (p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Shortage of information technologists forces schools for higher vocational education to seek remedy. (p11)
- Bus maker Berkhof Holding hopes to get Chinese order for 20 luxury coaches. (p11)
TROUW
- Aircrash in Brazil on October 30 forces Fokker to adjust 370 aircraft. (p3)
- Foodproducer Van Dijk takes over snacks maker Jongens Laan of Oostzaan. (p7)
